facts.statement: The genus Holonema was first described by Newberry in 1889.
Holonema was an extinct genus of large, barrel-shaped arthrodire placoderms.
facts.quote: Holonema is an extinct genus of relatively large, barrel-shaped arthrodire placoderms

facts.statement: Holonema fossils have been found in oceans worldwide during the Mid to Late Devonian periods.
facts.quote: found in oceans throughout the world from the Mid to Late Devonian

facts.statement: Researchers believe Holonema was a benthic-dwelling fish due to its cambered body shape.
facts.quote: Holonema is thought to have been a benthic-dwelling fish, based on its cambered body shape

facts.statement: Recent studies of the jaw and toothplates suggest Holonema likely had a planktivorous lifestyle.
facts.quote: more recent morphological studies of the jaw and toothplates suggest a more planktivorous lifestyle

facts.statement: Fossil Holonema individuals contained stones and feldspar pieces in their armor, suggesting they used these as gastroliths to aid digestion.
facts.quote: Holonema fossil individuals have small stones in the trunk shield, and pieces of feldspar in the abdominal region, suggesting Holonema used these as gastroliths for processing food

facts.statement: While most Holonema species are known only from armor fragments, H. westolli is known from complete, articulated specimens.
facts.quote: Most species of the genus are known from fragments of their armor, but the Gogo Reef species, H. westolli, is known from whole, articulated specimens

facts.statement: The species H. westolli reached a length of approximately 60.6 centimeters.
facts.quote: This species reached around 60.6 cm long

facts.statement: The median dorsal plate of H. radiatum averages about 30 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The median dorsal plate averages about 30 cm in length

facts.statement: The median dorsal plate of H. haiti is estimated to be about 28 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The median dorsal plate is estimated to be about 28 cm in length

facts.statement: The median dorsal plates of H. farrowi range up to 20 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The median dorsal plates range up to 20 cm in length

facts.statement: Holonema is classified within the class Placodermi.
Holonema belongs to the family Holonematidae.
Holonema lived from the Emsian to the Famennian, between 399.5 and 358.86 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Emsian to Famennian (399.5 to 358.86 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Holonema is Pterichthys rugosum.
H. obrutshevi is distinguished by a small, horn-like process on its median dorsal plate.
facts.quote: H. obrutshevi Found in the Eifelian-aged Aruküla beds of Estonia. The median dorsal plate has a small, horn-like process

facts.statement: H. harmae is distinguished by the spinal and subpectoral margins of its anterior-ventral plates meeting at almost a right angle.
facts.quote: H. harmae Found in the Givetian-aged Burtnieki beds of Estonia. It is distinguished from other species in that the spinal and subpectoral margins of the anterior-ventral plates meet at almost a right angle

facts.statement: H. haiti is known for having a very narrow median dorsal plate compared to other species.
facts.quote: H. haiti Known from fragments from the Givetian section of the Jefferson formation in Idaho. The median dorsal plate is estimated to be about 28 cm in length, and is very narrow compared to those of other species

facts.statement: It is debated whether H. ornatum belongs to the genus Holonema, as Denison (1978) suggested it might not.
facts.quote: Denison 1978 suggests that it may not belong to Holonema

rejected.statement: H. rugosum is a fairly large species, though the type specimen consists of an 18-centimeter long median dorsal plate from a small individual.
rejected.quote: It is a fairly large species, though the type specimen is of an 18 centimeter long median dorsal plate belonging to a small individual
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is a fairly large species though the type'

rejected.statement: H. rugosum was originally described as a species of the antiarch genus Pterichthys before being reclassified.
rejected.quote: H. rugosum is the type species. It was originally described as a species of the antiarch genus, Pterichthys
